newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy fixes 3pct limit for stakes in Stet.
newsitem.headline: Italy fixes 3pct limit for stakes in Stet.

text.p: Shareholders in Stet will be able to take a maximum three percent stake in the Italian telecoms group following its privatisation, slated for later this year, the Treasury said in a statement on Monday.

The Treasury added that it expected to hold a so-called 'golden share' in the company, which will give it special voting voting rights after it loses majority control, for up to three years following the sell-off.

The Treasury said the golden share would be dropped once the liberalisation of the domestic telecommunications market reached "a sufficiently advanced level" and when a watchdog body set up to oversee the sector consolidated its position.
"This might take less than three years, but it could take more," a spokeswoman at Stet said.

The golden share, following the procedure already established with energy group ENI, will give the state the right to veto new major shareholders; the right to veto any planned break-up of the group; and the right to a certain number of board members.
Italy has already said it wants to create a stable core of shareholders in Stet when control passes to private hands.
"The Treasury fixes three percent as the reference point for the exercising of special rights," Monday's statement said, adding three percent would also be the maximum holding.

Stet is due to be merged with its fixed-line telephony unit, Telecom Italia, later this year ahead of the much-delayed sale, now planned for October. But legislation needed for the sale, including a bill to create a watchdog body, has still not been approved by parliament and commentators say that, if the regulatory body has not been ratified by May, the sale might have to be postponed again.
